steps.message:
Using the hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers ladder — this lands on rung 1 (a field name others call), so I'm flagging the consequence before editing.

The change itself is one line, `routes/users.js:6`:

```js
users.map((u) => ({ userId: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email })),
```

But `README.md:3-5` states the contract explicitly:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

Renaming in place breaks all three consumers at once — including shipped iOS builds you can't redeploy and a partner export outside your control — and it bypasses the versioning rule the repo documents for exactly this change.

questions.question: GET /users has three external consumers and the README says field renames go through a versioned endpoint. How should I proceed?

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the documented rule: keep /users returning userId, add a versioned variant (e.g. /v2/users) that returns user_id. No consumer breaks; migration happens on each client's schedule. This is a design change, so I'd brainstorm the shape with you first.

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return userId and user_id side by side from /users. Unblocks new consumers on the snake_case name immediately, no breakage, and userId can be dropped once the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the partner export have all moved. Adds a duplicated field for a transition period.

options.label: Rename in place
options.description: Do exactly what was asked: change userId to user_id on line 6. This breaks the web app, shipped iOS clients, and the nightly partner export until each is updated. Choose this if those consumers are already handled or the contract note is stale.
